newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt warns against new EMU delay debate.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt warns against new EMU delay debate.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt on Monday spoke out against a new debate about delaying the start of European economic and monetary union (EMU).

"From the view of the German economy, a renewed delay debate is dangerous," he said in a statement. "The German business sector must be able to rely on the start date to be able to make the necessary preparations for the currency change-over on time."
A delay could hurt European economic development in the long term by upsetting currently stable inflation, interest and exchange rates, he said.
It would also "lead to uncertainty in international finance markets" and could hinder German exports and cost jobs, Rexrodt said.
At the same time, pushing back EMU from the planned launch in 1999 would set back Europe's integration policy, he said.

"In this deciding phase, we should not let doubts arise about a successful start of EMU on January 1, 1999," Rexrodt said. "That's why it is now up to us and our European partners to carry out the necessary steps to fulfil the convergence criteria with all decisiveness."
